settings.subtitle: Changes apply on the next poll cycle. Nothing here needs a restart.
settings.backup.label: Backup and migration
settings.backup.hint: Export everything on this page as a Light edition config.yml, or read one back in. Credentials travel as ${VARIABLE} references, never as values.
settings.retention.cost-estimated: ≈ {projected} of history, estimated · {current} on disk now

settings.timezone.label: Time zone
settings.timezone.hint: Clock times on this dashboard are shown in {zone}. Daily uptime bars stay on UTC days, which is how the samples are grouped.
settings.map-view.label: Geographic view
settings.map-view.hint: Shows monitored locations on the overview. Only providers that name their own regions or edge locations can be placed.
settings.routing.hint: The first rule that matches a change decides which channels hear about it.
routing.note: The first rule that matches a change decides which channels hear about it — rules below it are not consulted. Put the specific ones on top.
routing.empty: No rules — every change goes to every enabled channel, as before routing existed.
routing.shadowed: Never evaluated: rule {rule} above already matches everything this rule would.
routing.no-classes: No event classes selected — this rule can never fire.
routing.invalid_one: {count} saved rule could not be read and is being ignored. Check the container log.
routing.invalid_other: {count} saved rules could not be read and are being ignored. Check the container log.
routing.dryrun.title: If this happened
routing.dryrun.skipped.class: skipped, not this kind of event
routing.dryrun.none: No rule matches — nobody is notified
routing.dryrun.nobody: This rule targets a channel that is off — no channel will receive this
routing.dryrun.muted: Muted by rule {rule} — nobody is notified
field.adaptive.hint: While a provider has an open incident, poll it on the cadence below instead of its own.
field.confirm-samples.hint: Consecutive polls that must agree before a change is announced. One notifies immediately; more than one costs that many polls of delay and ignores a page that briefly disagrees with itself.
field.adaptive-interval.hint: Never slower than the provider’s own interval, so this can only watch it more closely.
field.interval.hint: Requests are staggered and the interval carries jitter, so providers are never hit in lockstep.
field.timeout.hint: A provider slower than this counts as a failed poll, not an outage.
field.retries.hint: Retries before a cycle is recorded as unreachable.
field.retention.hint: How long samples and incidents are kept before the daily prune takes them.
field.name: Name
chart.days-summary: Daily status over {count} days: {ok} operational, {issues} with issues, {unmeasured} not measured
chart.polls-summary: The last {count} polls: {ok} operational, {issues} with issues, {unmeasured} not measured
chart.trend-summary: Daily uptime over {count} days, between {min} and {max} percent
chart.trend-empty: Daily uptime over {count} days: nothing measured yet
catalog.label: Known providers
catalog.hint: Pick one to fill in the adapter and base URL, or paste a URL below and detect it.
catalog.empty: No bundled provider matches this filter — paste the URL below instead.
add.title: Add a service
add.subtitle: Most providers run on Atlassian Statuspage and need no code.
add.note.statuspage: The adapter appends /api/v2/summary.json to this URL.
add.note.instatus: Use the page's host, e.g. https://status.gcore.com; the adapter appends /summary.json to it.
add.note.betterstack: Use the page's host, e.g. https://status.betterstack.com; the adapter appends /index.json to it.
add.note.cachet: Use the Cachet instance's host, e.g. https://status.example.com; the adapter reads its /api/v1 endpoints.
add.note.uptimekuma: Give the status page URL, e.g. https://uptime.example.com/status/demo; the slug in it names the page.
add.note.uptimecom: Give the status page URL, e.g. https://status.uptime.com/statuspage/uptime-status; the adapter appends /ajax to it.
add.note.rss: Give the full URL of the RSS or Atom feed; the adapter reads it as given.
add.note.html: Give the full URL of the page to read; the adapter reads it as given.
add.note.slack: Use https://slack-status.com; the adapter appends /api/v2.0.0/current to it.
add.note.http: Give the full URL to probe; this check reads your own service, not a status page.
add.note.custom: The adapter reads this URL as given.
add.detect-ok: Reads as {adapter} — adapter and base URL filled in.
add.detect-none: No known adapter recognised this page. Pick one below.
scrape.warning: Reading a page's markup breaks silently when the page changes. A selector that stops matching is reported as a failing provider, never as "operational".
scrape.selector-hint: The element whose text says how the provider is, e.g. .status-banner or #status > h2. Tag, #id, .class and [attr] with the descendant and child combinators.
scrape.words-hint: Comma-separated, per severity. Leave a severity empty to keep the built-in words for it; the longest match on the page wins.
probe.warning: This check reads your own endpoint from this machine. Everything it can reach, it will probe — and a network failure here reads as every probed service being down at once.
probe.path-hint: Appended to the URL above, verbatim. Use it when the endpoint needs a trailing slash, which the URL field drops.
probe.expect-status-hint: Single codes or inclusive ranges, comma-separated. Anything else reads as an outage.
probe.expect-body-hint: Plain text, matched anywhere in the response. Leave empty to check the status alone.
probe.absent-body-hint: How an error page served with a healthy status line is caught.
probe.slow-ms-hint: An answer this slow or slower reads degraded instead of operational. Leave empty for no threshold.
probe.tls-warn-days-hint: A certificate expiring within this many days reads degraded. Costs a second connection per poll, so leave it empty to skip the check.
probe.header-hint: One optional request header, e.g. Authorization. Write a secret as ${VAR} — the value is read from the environment, never stored here.
components.hint: Optional: with none selected, only the overall status is monitored
components.scope-hint: Incidents attributed only to other components are ignored, and the status shown is the worst of the selection. A notice the provider attaches to no component stays reported.
channel.summary.none: No channel is on — a status change would notify nobody.
channel.secret-saved: Credential saved — in use right away, no restart needed.
push.enabled: This browser will now receive notifications.
push.registered-channel-off: This browser is registered, but the channel is off — enable it above to actually receive notifications.
push.denied: Notifications are blocked for this site in the browser's settings.
push.push-service-brave: Brave blocked the registration with its push service, which it disables by default. Open brave://settings/privacy, turn on “Use Google services for push messaging”, restart Brave, then enable this browser again.
push.push-service: The browser could not register with its push service. It is usually turned off in the browser's own settings (Brave and some Chromium builds ship it off) or blocked upstream by a firewall, VPN or DNS filter — allow it, restart the browser, then try again.
push.unsupported: This browser cannot receive push notifications here. Open the dashboard on localhost or over HTTPS.
map.title: Where the fleet is
map.error: The map could not be loaded.
map.empty_one: No component has a known location · 1 could not be placed
map.empty_other: No component has a known location · {count} could not be placed
map.footnote_one: {count} component located · {unplaced} could not be placed
map.footnote_other: {count} components located · {unplaced} could not be placed
field.group-hint: Providers in the same group get a combined status, and one routing rule can cover all of them. Leave empty for none.
field.provider-interval-hint: Minutes between polls of this provider. Leave empty to follow the global interval.
add.note.aws: Use https://health.aws.amazon.com; the adapter appends /public/currentevents to it.
add.note.gcp: Use https://status.cloud.google.com; the adapter appends /incidents.json to it.
add.note.azure: Use https://azure.status.microsoft; the adapter appends /en-us/status/feed/ to it.
delivery.subtitle: Every notification IsItDown tried to send, delivered or not.
delivery.empty-failed: No failed deliveries — every notification got through.
settings.removed-note: A removed provider keeps its history until the restore window closes. After that the removal is permanent.
providers.remove-restorable: It leaves the dashboard now. Its history is kept for a few days, and the removal can be undone from Settings until then.
settings.delivery.note: How much of what the rules admit actually goes out, and in how many messages. Everything here is off by default.
field.quiet-hours.hint: During the window below, only changes at or above the floor are sent. Anything under it is dropped, not deferred.
field.quiet-hours.zone.hint: The zone the window above is read in. “Server” uses the zone the container runs in.
field.digest.hint: Collect changes under the floor and send them as one message per window. Anything at or above the floor is still sent the moment it happens.
field.cap.hint: At most this many messages an hour per provider. What the cap hides is counted and reported in the next message that gets through.
field.update-in-place.hint: An incident’s updates rewrite the message its opening sent, on channels that can edit one (Telegram, Discord). Others still get a message per update.
routing.dryrun.quiet-note: Evaluated with the quiet-hours window as it stands now.
adapter.debug.title: Adapter diagnostics
adapter.debug.description: The last reads of this provider’s page, and what the adapter makes of it right now.
adapter.debug.empty: No read recorded yet — this provider has not been polled since the container started.
adapter.debug.unknown-warning: The page was read but nothing recognisable was found in it — for a scrape, the selector probably no longer matches.
